headline: Foggy, dry Friday night; light rain Saturday; stormy, breezy stretch Monday into Tuesday.
summary: A high-pressure ridge aloft keeps western Washington mostly dry tonight, though fog and low clouds form in valleys and lowlands. That ridge weakens over the weekend as a low settles offshore and wanders along the coast. Saturday brings light rain to the lowlands and snow showers to the mountains, with no major impacts expected. Next week turns stormy: a broad trough over the northeast Pacific sends a series of storm systems toward Washington, with a stronger one arriving Monday night into Tuesday. It brings widespread rain, gusty winds, high seas, and possible minor coastal flooding at high tides, and the Skokomish River is likely to reach flood stage later next week. Forecasters are less sure about the timing and strength of those systems.
changes: Forecasters softened the overnight fog forecast, since models are backing off and satellite images show breaks in the clouds. Confidence in strong winds and high seas Monday into Tuesday has grown.
